title: Customer VPC Onboarding Playbook — Terraform + Upgrade Notes (draft)
content:
Purpose
This is a working draft playbook for onboarding customer VPCs for Redwood Private (VPC + on-prem) installations. It combines network reference patterns, Terraform module notes, and a stepwise upgrade/rollback plan. Use this as the canonical checklist for SE/solutions + infra teams during pre-sales and early deployment.

High level goals
- Provide repeatable, low-friction onboarding for customers that want Redwood Private in their VPC (AWS) or air-gapped on-prem variant.
- Minimize blast radius during upgrades; provide quick rollback and post-upgrade verification steps.
- Capture Terraform module caveats and recommended provider patterns for multi-account setups.

Who should use this
- Solutions Engineers leading handoffs
- Platform/Infra engineers performing the initial deployment
- Customer SREs during acceptance testing and upgrades

Quick reference: VPC topologies supported
1) Single-account VPC (small customers) — all components in customer VPC, PrivateLink for control plane if required.
2) Transit/Hub VPC (recommended for enterprises) — customer Transit Gateway or hub VPC connects a dedicated Redwood workload VPC; uses VGW/Transit attachments for cross-account routing.
3) Peered multi-account VPCs — limited to simple networks and non-overlapping CIDRs; avoid for high-throughput workloads.
4) On-prem (air-gapped) — physical network diagram required; local KMS/HSM; internal DNS + NTP; no outbound connectivity to Redwood control plane unless requested.

Network checklist (pre-deploy)
- Confirm non-overlapping CIDR blocks: request 10.100.0.0/16 or similar for Redwood workload VPC.
- Required subnets: public-bastion (optional), private-app (multiple AZs), gpu-pool (if customer provides GPUs), management-subnet for control-plane endpoints.
- Routing: route tables per AZ; ensure NAT gateway or egress path for required package repos (if allowed). Document any restricted egress (proxy IPs).
- Firewall & SGs: inbound only from bastion and control-plane endpoints; ephemeral ports for gRPC/token comms; explicit ports in appendix.
- DNS: plan for private hosted zone (Route 53) or use customer's internal DNS. Provide FQDNs for internal components (e.g., private-api.redwood.internal).
- KMS/HSM: confirm key policy, principal ARNs for Redwood infra IAM role.
- Monitoring/logging: S3 bucket or SIEM endpoint for metrics and audit logs; ensure bucket policy allows our service-account principal.
- Time sync: NTP allowed or local NTP server provided.

Terraform module notes (implementation guidance)
- Repo: github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules (see linked PRs).
- Provider strategy: use provider aliases for multi-account (provider "aws" { region = var.region } provider "aws" { alias = "customer" region = var.customer_region }). Avoid dynamic provider creation at runtime; define alias per account to keep plan/apply deterministic.
- Remote state: recommend S3 backend + DynamoDB locking in the customer account for the customer-managed stack; for Redwood-managed pieces use our remote state bucket with strict IAM roles.
- Module inputs to standardize: vpc_cidr, public_subnets, private_subnets, azs, enable_transit_gateway (bool), control_plane_endpoints (list), kms_key_arn. Keep default tags and naming prefix variables to avoid collisions.
- State scoping: split state into logical units: network.tfstate, infra.tfstate, routing.tfstate. This reduces contention and allows partial rollbacks.
- Example snippet (conceptual):
  module "redwood_vpc" {
    source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules//vpc?ref=main"
    vpc_cidr = var.vpc_cidr
    public_subnets = var.public_subnets
    private_subnets = var.private_subnets
    tags = var.tags
  }
- Secrets handling: do not place secrets in TF state; use SSM Parameter Store or secrets manager with rotation policies. For air-gapped, provide an encrypted file bundle that the customer loads into their secrets store.
- Version pinning: pin module versions and provider versions in root module (terraform { required_version = ">= 1.3" required_providers { aws = { version = "~> 5.0" } } }). Record module versions in onboarding ticket.

Common Terraform gotchas we've seen
- Overlapping security_group rules created by multiple modules — recommend central SG management module.
- VPC CIDR changes mid-deploy cause resource replacement; encourage customers to finalize CIDR ahead of time.
- Cross-account role assumption requires correct "sts:AssumeRole" policy and external_id handling. Test with a minimal script before full apply.

Onboarding playbook (step-by-step)
1) Pre-engagement (solutions)
   - Collect network worksheet: CIDRs, preferred AZs, KMS ARN, SIEM S3 bucket, proxy egress rules.
   - Raise internal ticket and link PRs/Confluence architecture.
2) Kickoff (customer + SE + infra)
   - Walk through topology, required IAM roles, and acceptance tests.
3) Create terraform plan in a sandbox account
   - Run `terraform init` and `terraform plan` with staging vars. Share plan with customer.
4) Customer review & approvals
   - Customer verifies IAM and networking changes; confirm maintenance windows for route updates.
5) Apply (maintenance window)
   - Apply network module first, then infra. Keep a single engineer on-call to watch CloudWatch/metrics.
6) Smoke tests (automated)
   - DNS resolution, internal API ping, token issuance, basic training sample run (< 1k tokens).
7) Harden (1–2 days post deploy)
   - Lockdown SGs, remove temporary open rules, rotate any test keys, enable audit collection.

Upgrade plan (minor and major releases)
- Minor (patch/minor): can be automated via CI with canary rollout to 1 AZ/workload. Steps: run terraform plan, apply to canary, run smoke tests, expand to remaining AZs.
- Major (breaking): requires blue/green or full maintenance window. Create a staging cluster with new version, run compatibility tests, and switch routing via terraform-managed DNS or LB.

Pre-upgrade checklist
- Backup TF state, snapshot any EBS volumes, export DB dumps if present.
- Confirm image and runtime compatibility matrix (appendix B).
- Capture current KPIs (latency, throughput, error rates).

Rollback plan
- If post-upgrade verification fails: revert terraform to prior versioned state (use `terraform state pull` to validate), run `terraform apply` with previous module versions and state snapshot.
- If cluster-level rollback required: use previously-saved AMI/helm chart release; avoid in-place config rewrites.

Post-upgrade validation (automated suite)
- Endpoint health, authentication flow, end-to-end sample prompt suite comparing token-level outputs, latency p95/p99, cost per token estimate.

Appendices
A: Ports and endpoints (customer-facing list)\- 443: control-plane TLS\- 2200: optional bastion SSH\- 50051: internal gRPC (restrict to SGs)\- DNS: internal hosted zone details

B: Compatibility matrix (summary)\- Redwood Private v2.x: requires k8s >= 1.25, nvidia-driver >= 525, CUDA 12.x.\- Older nodes: contact infra to plan node replacement.

C: Example Jira/Confluence checklist (templates in linked artifacts)

Unresolved questions / TODOs (action items)
- Decide default MTU for hybrid networks (1500 vs 9001) — Mei to validate with infra team.
- Finalize provider alias pattern for the cross-account staging flow.
- Add automated Terraform preflight script to verify IAM trust/policies before apply (PR referenced in linked_artifacts).

Notes to self
- Keep this doc lightweight; move final-runbooks into Confluence after 2 successful onboardings.
- Get legal signoff on access patterns for customer-managed S3 buckets.

If you're running an onboarding this week, ping the #eng-private-deployments channel and reference this doc + the linked PR for the latest module version.
